sections.h2: How quickly can a Yorktown house change hands?
sections.html:
Sellers here pick between a broker, a sale on their own, or a cash buyer who accepts the house unchanged. Yorktown sits on the northern edge of Westchester County, about 38 miles from midtown Manhattan. It is a town, so you deal with the receiver of taxes, the assessor and the building inspector in place of a city hall.

The town is made up of five business hamlets, and no train runs inside its borders. Buyers weigh commute time, school district and the age of the mechanical systems, which makes the records you can hand over early the main factor in closing speed.

Owners dominate and incomes are high. The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 35,944 people, 1.7 percent below the 2020 base of 36,562.

Nearly 95 percent of residents stayed put over the past year, so many owners have long tenures. Commuters head to the nearest Metro-North stations, in Katonah on the Harlem Line and Peekskill on the Hudson Line.

Putnam Valley in Putnam County bounds the town on the north, Somers on the east, New Castle on the south and Cortlandt on the west. The Croton River crosses the south end.

  • Yorktown Heights, the mailing address of Town Hall.
  • Jefferson Valley, site of the Jefferson Valley Mall.
  • Shrub Oak, Mohegan Lake and Crompond, part of which lies in Cortlandt.

Franklin D. Roosevelt State Park and the North County Trailway, built on the old New York and Putnam rail bed, are the best known open spaces and worth naming in a listing.

School levy depends on which of four districts your parcel is in. Yorktown Central covers a large part of town, and the rest goes to Lakeland Central, Croton-Harmon Union Free or Ossining Union Free.

The town receiver collects school tax on behalf of all four but has no say over their budgets. Confirm the district before you list, and tell buyers which one applies.

sections.h2: Older houses and the systems buyers check
sections.html: Snow load, repeated freezing and thawing and long cold spells put the roof, driveway and heating plant at the top of an inspection list. A house with a recent furnace and roof, and the receipts to show it, will present better than one without.

The Receiver of Taxes collects what the town levies, including fire, parks, sewer and water districts, together with county and school tax. Owners receive two bills a year, and a bill that fails to arrive does not cancel the obligation.

  • School tax, July 1 to June 30: one bill is mailed September 1 with two stubs. Half is due September 30 and half January 31, and a weekend due date rolls to the next business day, which puts the 2027 second half on February 1.
  • School penalties on the first half: 2 percent in October, 5 percent in November, 7 percent in December and January, 10 percent in February and March, 12 percent afterward until sale.
  • Town and county tax: mailed April 1, due April 30. Penalties run 2 percent in May, 5 percent in June and July, 7 percent in August and September, 10 percent from October through December and 12 percent after that.

The second school half draws no penalty through January and 10 percent in February and March. No reminder notices go out in January, and the town has no authority to waive penalties. A mailed payment needs a genuine post office postmark by the due date. Machine postmarks reflect the day mail is first processed at a regional facility, so mail well ahead. The Tax Office at 363 Underhill Avenue keeps weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and a green drop box sits behind Town Hall.

Applications are accepted from June 1 through Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of June. For the 2027 roll the cutoff is 8 p.m. on June 15, 2027, and the Board of Assessment Review sits at Town Hall that evening from 4 to 8 p.m. Filing is free and needs no attorney.

Support your case with sales of similar houses in your neighborhood and school district within a year of the July 1, 2026 valuation date, or with an appraisal. Email filings are refused. Hand-delivery, mail, FedEx, UPS and the drop box at the rear entrance of Town Hall are accepted, and the board mails its determination on September 15, 2027.

The assessor also examines each transfer of property, noting buyer, seller and price. Common exemptions include senior citizens, STAR, military service and agricultural. Call 914-962-5722, extension 2.

The Building Inspector applies the town's zoning ordinance and the State building codes, writes permits and certificates of occupancy, and can authorize condemnation of unsafe buildings. Applications filed on or after December 31, 2025 are measured against the 2025 editions of the State codes. Hours are weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall.

The town warns that it never tells anyone to wire a development fee. Fees are paid by check to the Town of Yorktown under the master fee schedule.

Yorktown buyers tend to be careful about the age of the house, so a folder of records helps. Collect permits and certificates of occupancy from the Building Department, the receipts for the roof and furnace, and the latest school and town bills. The Tax Office can confirm what is paid, and the assessor can tell you which exemptions the parcel carries.

A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal and takes the house as it stands, so repairs are off your list. The tax payoff, the transfer forms and the county recording still apply, so ask your attorney to prepare them while you collect the paperwork.

Recording is done by the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk, which requires four items prepared in the clerk's PREP portal: a recording cover page, a TP-584, an RP-5217 and a payment cover page.

The state transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500, and it is payable when the deed is presented. The seller pays unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. A residence at $1 million or more adds a 1 percent buyer's tax.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Yorktown school tax due?
faqs.a: January 31. A weekend date moves to the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due Monday, February 1.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to Yorktown town and county tax paid in June?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5 percent. The bill is due April 30, adds 2 percent in May and 5 percent in June and July, and the town says it cannot waive any of it.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Yorktown assessment?
faqs.a: File with the Assessment Office between June 1 and Grievance Day, which is June 15, 2027, attaching comparable sales or an appraisal. The office takes no email filings.

faqs.q: Which Yorktown office issues certificates of occupancy?
faqs.a: The Building Department at Town Hall, 363 Underhill Avenue, headed by the Building Inspector, who also issues permits and enforces zoning and State codes.

faqs.q: Who pays state transfer tax on a Yorktown sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500.
